issues.line_text: Roy glanced toward the cottage. Eleanor's car wasn't thereΓÇöshe'd gone to town for supplies. We were alone.
issues.description: Eleanor doesn't have a car mentioned in the Story Bible. She walks/runs everywhere. This is the only reference to 'Eleanor's car' in the manuscript.
issues.fix: Roy glanced toward the cottage. Eleanor wasn't aroundΓÇöshe'd gone to town for supplies. We were alone.
issues.rationale: Removes the car reference while maintaining the scene's purpose (Josh and Roy alone to discuss David Park). Consistent with Eleanor's established transportation methods.

issues.line_text: Eleanor wasn't here yet. She only started earlier this year.
issues.description: Roy says Eleanor 'only started earlier this year' (2024) but Story Bible states Eleanor claims 6 months tenure (since ~April 2024), and Josh already knows this claim from the rental listing. The phrasing 'earlier this year' is vague and could mean January-March, contradicting the April timeline.
issues.fix: Eleanor wasn't here yet. She only started in the spring.
issues.rationale: Spring is more consistent with April 2024 start date. Maintains Roy's knowledge while avoiding specific month contradiction.

issues.line_text: The call came on a gray November afternoon.
issues.description: Timeline tracking: Josh goes to clinic, nurse says 'two days' for results, then 'The call came on a gray November afternoon.' But no specific date is given for when he went to the clinic. Given the chapter spans Nov 15-17, this scene likely occurs Nov 17, but should be clearer.
issues.fix: The call came two days later, on a gray November afternoon.
issues.rationale: Clarifies the two-day wait mentioned by the nurse, maintaining timeline consistency without requiring a specific date.

issues.line_text:
The measurements. The hunting observations.

Her. The winter one. YoungΓÇöearly twenties. Alone up here. Trusting.

Not Eleanor. Someone else. Someone from before.
issues.description: This passage reveals Josh is reading notes about a previous victim ('the winter one' = Lily, killed Feb 2020). The phrase 'Someone from before' combined with 'winter' and 'early twenties' makes it too obvious Josh has been here before and killed someone. This is a protected twist (Josh doesn't know he killed Lily until Chapter 25).
issues.fix:
The measurements. The surveillance notes.

Details about the property. Weather patterns. Security gaps.

Not current observations. Something from another time.
issues.rationale: Maintains the unsettling discovery that Josh has older files he doesn't remember writing, but removes the explicit 'hunting' language and victim description that spoils his connection to Lily's murder.

issues.line_text: I looked at my hands. Wondered if they'd taken medication I didn't recall. Wondered what else they'd done that I couldn't remember.
issues.description: This line comes dangerously close to Josh suspecting himself of violence. While some self-doubt is appropriate in Act 2, this specific formulation ('what else they'd done') suggests potential violent acts, which is premature for Chapter 11 (still Act 1/early Act 2).
issues.fix: I looked at my hands. Wondered if they'd taken medication I didn't recall. Wondered what else I was forgetting.
issues.rationale: Maintains Josh's concern about memory gaps without the violent implication. 'What I was forgetting' is general enough to preserve tension without spoiling that he's capable of violence.

notes: Chapter 11 is generally clean. The toxic testing scene is well-handledΓÇöambiguous results maintain tension without confirming drugging. The David Park revelation (victim who stayed at Thornewood) is a good plant. The 'voice inside my head' ending effectively sets up dissociative episodes without being too explicit. Main issues are: (1) car reference inconsistency, (2) one critical spoiler about previous victim observations, (3) timeline clarity needed for clinic results, (4) minor self-suspicion language that's slightly premature for Act 1/2 boundary.
